analysis.overall: You had a solid day overall with 82% time in range, though a late-night meal caused an extended high peak while you slept.

events.title: Late dinner spike
events.description: A 65g carb meal late in the evening sent glucose climbing past 200 mg/dL over the next two hours.

events.title: Overnight correction phase
events.description: Multiple small correction boluses overnight gradually coaxed glucose back down into range, reaching normal levels by early morning.

events.title: Rock-solid morning flatline
events.description: Glucose stayed exceptionally stable in the 90-100 mg/dL range throughout the entire early morning.

events.title: Brunch bolus and quick recovery
events.description: Bolusing at 96 mg/dL for 50g of carbs led to a modest peak of 163 mg/dL before bringing you cleanly back down to 91 mg/dL.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Keep an eye on how late meals impact overnight trends—heavier dinners closer to bed seem to take several hours to come back down.
